subject: science
prompt: Throughout the day, the position of a tree's shadow changes. In the morning, the shadow is long and points one way. By noon, the shadow is short. By late afternoon, the shadow is long again and points the opposite direction. Which best explains why the shadow's position and length change during the day?
optionA: Earth rotates on its axis
optionB: The atmosphere becomes thicker as the sun sets
optionC: The sun moves around Earth
optionD: The sun gets closer to Earth during the day
explanation: As Earth rotates on its axis, different parts of Earth face the sun at different times, causing the sun to appear to move across the sky. This makes shadows change position and length throughout the day.
factClaim: Earth's rotation on its axis causes the sun to appear to move across the sky during the day.

subject: science
prompt: A student shines a laser pointer through two clear plastic tubes. One tube is perfectly straight. The other tube is bent in the middle like an elbow. Through which tube, if any, will the laser light be visible on a screen beyond the tube?
optionA: Through the straight tube only, because light travels in a straight line
optionB: Through the bent tube only, because the curve helps focus the light
optionC: Through both tubes, because light can bounce around any shape
optionD: Through neither tube, because the plastic absorbs the light
explanation: Light travels in straight lines and cannot turn corners. The laser light will only pass through the straight tube and reach the screen; the bent tube will block the light path.
factClaim: Light travels in straight lines and cannot follow a curved path through bent tubes.

subject: science
prompt: A student places different small objects in a bucket of water and watches to see which ones float: a pencil, an eraser, a plastic bead, a stone pebble, a piece of aluminum foil, and honey (in a sealed container). Which set of items will float because they are less dense than water?
optionA: Pencil, plastic bead, honey
optionB: Eraser, stone pebble, plastic bead
optionC: Stone pebble, eraser, honey
optionD: Pencil, aluminum foil, stone pebble
explanation: Objects float when they are less dense than water. Pencils (mostly wood), plastic beads, and honey-filled containers are all less dense than water, so they will float. Stone and erasers sink because they are denser than water.
factClaim: Objects less dense than water will float; objects more dense than water will sink.

subject: science
prompt: A food chain is shown: clover plants → rabbits → foxes → eagles. What role do the clover plants have in this food chain?
optionA: They capture energy from the sun and provide food for consumers
optionB: They prevent eagles from eating too many foxes
optionC: They break down dead organisms into simpler substances
optionD: They eat the sun's energy and pass it to consumers
explanation: Clover plants are producers that capture the sun's energy through photosynthesis. They convert this energy into plant matter, which serves as food for consumers like rabbits further up the food chain.
factClaim: Producers are plants that capture energy from the sun and serve as the base of the food chain.

subject: science
prompt: A student sets up two identical wet cloths outdoors: one is placed in front of a strong fan, and the other is placed in direct sunlight. Both start wet but the student wants to find which dries faster. Which two forms of energy are being compared in this investigation?
optionA: Mechanical energy and thermal energy
optionB: Sound energy and thermal energy
optionC: Light energy and electrical energy
optionD: Electrical energy and sound energy
explanation: The fan provides mechanical energy (moving air) to carry away moisture, while the sun provides thermal energy (heat) to speed up water evaporation. By comparing these two, the student can see which form of energy more effectively dries the cloth.
factClaim: Mechanical energy from moving air and thermal energy from heat both accelerate the rate of evaporation.

subject: science
prompt: A table shows information about five vegetables and the time they need to grow: Lettuce (5 days to sprout, 30-40 days to harvest), Tomato (8-10 days to sprout, 60-85 days to harvest), Carrot (10-14 days to sprout, 65-80 days to harvest), Spinach (5-7 days to sprout, 40-50 days to harvest), Pumpkin (7-10 days to sprout, 90-120 days to harvest). Which statement is supported by the data?
optionA: Lettuce is ready for harvest in less time than spinach
optionB: Pumpkins take the least time overall because their seeds are large
optionC: Carrots sprout fastest of all the vegetables
optionD: Spinach needs more total time to harvest than tomatoes
explanation: According to the table, lettuce takes 30-40 days to harvest, while spinach takes 40-50 days. Lettuce is therefore ready for harvest sooner than spinach.
factClaim: Lettuce reaches harvest in less total time (30-40 days) compared to spinach (40-50 days).

subject: science
topic: Relative distances of planets from the sun
prompt: A student builds a model of the solar system in the gymnasium, with the clock on the wall representing the sun. The student must place model planets at their correct distances from the sun. Which planet should be placed at the greatest distance from the clock?
optionA: Venus
optionB: Saturn
optionC: Jupiter
optionD: Neptune
explanation: Neptune is the farthest planet from the sun in our solar system. In a scale model of the solar system, Neptune would need to be placed at the greatest distance from the sun representation.
factClaim: Neptune is the farthest planet from the sun in our solar system.

subject: science
prompt: A student observes a young hamster in a cage and records: it grooms its fur by licking its paws, it runs on its exercise wheel, it pushes food pellets into its cheek pouches, it eats from a food dish that the student sets out daily. Which observation is most likely a LEARNED behavior rather than an instinctive one?
optionA: Grooming its fur by licking its paws
optionB: Running on the exercise wheel
optionC: Pushing food into its cheek pouches
optionD: Eating from a specific food dish provided by the student
explanation: Hamsters have instinctive behaviors like grooming, running, and storing food in their cheeks. However, eating from a specific dish is a learned behavior because the hamster must learn to find and use the particular food dish the student provides.
factClaim: Learned behaviors are acquired through experience or training, while instinctive behaviors are inborn.

subject: science
prompt: A student reads the definition: 'the process by which water vapor in the air cools and turns into liquid water droplets.' Which term describes this process in the water cycle?
optionA: Evaporation
optionB: Precipitation
optionC: Sublimation
optionD: Condensation
explanation: Condensation is the process where water vapor in the atmosphere cools and transforms into liquid water droplets, forming clouds and dew.
factClaim: Condensation is the water cycle process where water vapor cools and becomes liquid water.

subject: science
prompt: A marine biologist studies dolphins in the ocean and gathers these observations: dolphins can echo-locate using sound waves, dolphins swim in warm ocean currents, dolphins hunt and eat fish, dolphins rest on sandy ocean bottoms. Which observation describes dolphins interacting with a LIVING element of their ecosystem?
optionA: Dolphins swim in warm ocean currents
optionB: Dolphins can echo-locate using sound waves
optionC: Dolphins rest on sandy ocean bottoms
optionD: Dolphins hunt and eat fish
explanation: Biotic interactions involve living things. Hunting and eating fish is a living interaction because both dolphins and fish are living organisms. Currents and sandy bottoms are abiotic (non-living) parts of the environment.
factClaim: Biotic interactions are between living organisms; hunting and eating other fish is an example of a biotic interaction.

subject: science
prompt: Four examples of objects or activities using different types of energy: Example 1) spinning bicycle wheels, Example 2) burning wood in a fireplace, Example 3) pushing a moving swing higher, Example 4) a robot arm lifting a box. Which examples use MECHANICAL energy to perform their function?
optionA: Examples 1, 2, and 4
optionB: Examples 1, 3, and 4
optionC: Examples 2 and 3 only
optionD: Examples 1 and 2 only
explanation: Mechanical energy is energy of motion. Spinning wheels (1), pushing a swing (3), and a robot arm lifting (4) all use motion-based mechanical energy. Burning wood (2) is chemical energy released as thermal energy.
factClaim: Mechanical energy is the energy associated with motion and moving objects.

subject: science
prompt: A hummingbird has a long, thin, pointed beak for sipping nectar from flowers. A woodpecker has a strong, thick beak for pecking through bark to find insects. The difference between the shapes of their beaks is most likely related to the:
optionA: Different parts of the forest where they live
optionB: Different sizes of the birds
optionC: Different predators that hunt them
optionD: Different ways they find and eat their food
explanation: The beak structure of each bird is adapted to how it obtains food. Hummingbirds need long beaks to drink nectar, while woodpeckers need strong beaks to drill for insects. This structural difference directly relates to their feeding methods.
factClaim: Structural adaptations like beak shape are related to an animal's feeding method and food sources.

subject: science
prompt: A student is classifying materials. Answering which question will provide the BEST evidence that an unknown object is a metal?
optionA: Does the object have a shiny appearance?
optionB: How much does the object weigh?
optionC: Does the object conduct (transfer) thermal energy quickly?
optionD: How quickly does the object dissolve in water?
explanation: Metals are excellent conductors of thermal energy. This property is fundamental to metals and distinguishes them from most other materials. While shininess and weight vary, thermal conductivity is a reliable identifying property of metals.
factClaim: Metals conduct thermal energy very well, which is a key identifying property.

subject: science
prompt: A biologist observes a squirrel in a park and records these observations: 1) climbing the tree trunk, 2) eating acorns from an oak tree, 3) burying acorns in the soil, 4) running across the ground, 5) drinking water from a puddle, 6) startled by a passing hawk. Which TWO observations best describe how the squirrel interacts with LIVING parts of its environment?
optionA: Observations 4 and 5
optionB: Observations 2 and 6
optionC: Observations 1 and 3
optionD: Observations 3 and 5
explanation: Biotic interactions involve living organisms. Eating acorns (2) is an interaction with a living tree, and being startled by a hawk (6) is an interaction with another living animal. The other observations involve non-living elements like soil, water, and the ground.
factClaim: Biotic interactions occur between living organisms, such as predator-prey relationships and feeding on living plants.

subject: science
prompt: A student pours 8 grams of salt into a jar containing 250 milliliters of water and stirs for one minute. Which change most likely occurs to the salt when added to the water?
optionA: The salt breaks down to form new substances
optionB: The salt turns the water into a different liquid
optionC: The salt completely dissolves to form a saltwater solution
optionD: The salt floats on the surface of the water
explanation: When salt dissolves in water, it mixes uniformly throughout the water to form a solution. This is a physical change, not a chemical change, because no new substances are created—only the distribution of salt particles in water.
factClaim: Dissolving is a physical change where a solid mixes uniformly with a liquid to form a solution.

subject: science
topic: Refraction of light through a lens
prompt: A student looks at a small insect through a magnifying glass lens. Which statement describes what happens to the light rays as they pass through the magnifying glass?
optionA: Light travels through the lens without changing direction
optionB: Light travels in straight lines and cannot be affected by the lens
optionC: Light bends (refracts) as it passes through the curved lens
optionD: Light bounces off the lens and cannot pass through
explanation: When light passes through a curved lens like a magnifying glass, it bends (refracts). This bending of light rays is what allows the lens to magnify objects, making them appear larger.
factClaim: Light refracts (bends) when passing through a curved lens, enabling magnification.

subject: science
prompt: A student lists different energy sources used to generate electricity: Solar power, Natural gas, Geothermal energy, Oil, Tidal power. Which of these sources are RENEWABLE resources?
optionA: Solar power, geothermal energy, and tidal power
optionB: Natural gas, oil, and solar power
optionC: Solar power and oil only
optionD: Natural gas, geothermal energy, and tidal power
explanation: Renewable resources naturally replenish and do not run out. Solar power (from the sun), geothermal energy (from Earth's heat), and tidal power (from ocean tides) are all renewable. Natural gas and oil are non-renewable fossil fuels.
factClaim: Renewable energy sources replenish naturally and include solar, geothermal, and tidal power.

subject: science
prompt: Bees have long, brush-like structures on their legs for collecting pollen. Beetles also have similar brush-like structures on their legs. Which statement best describes why bees and beetles both have these structures?
optionA: Both insects are the same size and shape
optionB: Both insects have the same predators
optionC: Both insects use the structures to collect the same food source: pollen
optionD: Both insects migrate to the same locations each year
explanation: Bees and beetles both interact with flowers and pollen as a food source. Their similar brush-like structures (called pollen baskets in bees, scopae in beetles) are adaptations for collecting and carrying pollen from flowers.
factClaim: Structural adaptations that are similar across different species often serve the same purpose, such as collecting food.

subject: science
topic: Testing for iron with a magnet
prompt: A student grinds a sample of an unknown mineral into a fine powder, mixes it with water, and then holds a magnet near the mixture. The student observes that some of the powder sticks to the magnet. Which conclusion is most supported by this observation?
optionA: The mineral contains copper
optionB: The mineral contains iron
optionC: The mineral contains aluminum
optionD: The mineral contains salt
explanation: Iron and its compounds are magnetic and are attracted to magnets. When the powder sticks to the magnet, it indicates the presence of iron in the mineral. This is a simple and effective way to test for iron.
factClaim: Iron is a magnetic element and will be attracted to a magnet, providing evidence of its presence.

subject: science
prompt: The taiga biome has extremely cold winters with temperatures dropping to -40°C or lower, moderate snowfall, short summers, and evergreen forests. Based on these characteristics, which pair of animals is LEAST likely to live in the taiga?
optionA: Moose and lynx
optionB: Elk and black bear
optionC: Flamingo and crocodile
optionD: Porcupine and wolf
explanation: Flamingos are tropical wading birds and crocodiles are warm-water reptiles; both require warm climates and would not survive the extreme cold of the taiga. Moose, lynx, elk, bears, porcupines, and wolves are all adapted to cold forests.
factClaim: Animals are adapted to specific biomes; tropical animals like flamingos and crocodiles cannot survive in cold taiga biomes.

subject: science
prompt: A student creates a model showing Earth (a globe), the sun (a lamp), and the moon (a ball) to demonstrate the cycle of day and night. Which action should the student perform with the model objects to show one complete day-night cycle on Earth?
optionA: Move the lamp around the globe once
optionB: Move the moon around the globe once
optionC: Spin the globe on its axis once
optionD: Move the globe around the lamp once
explanation: One complete day-night cycle is caused by Earth rotating on its axis one full time. Spinning the globe once on its axis will demonstrate this rotation and show how different parts of Earth experience day and night.
factClaim: One rotation of Earth on its axis creates one complete day-night cycle.

subject: science
prompt: Paleontologists discover fossils of coral reefs in rock layers deep underground in the middle of a desert. Modern-day coral reefs only grow in warm, shallow ocean water. What does this fossil discovery suggest about the history of this desert region?
optionA: The area has always been a dry desert
optionB: The area was once covered by a warm, shallow ocean or sea
optionC: Humans brought coral to this location thousands of years ago
optionD: The area was once extremely cold and covered with glaciers
explanation: Fossil corals only form in warm ocean environments. The presence of coral fossils in a desert indicates that this area was once underwater with warm ocean conditions, which has since changed dramatically.
factClaim: Fossils provide evidence of past environmental conditions; coral fossils indicate the area was once a warm ocean.

subject: science
prompt: Which land formation is correctly paired with the geological force that created it?
optionA: A deep canyon was formed by wind erosion over time
optionB: A volcanic mountain was formed by a river cutting through rock
optionC: A river delta was formed by glaciers moving across land
optionD: A deep valley was carved by a river flowing and cutting through rock layers
explanation: Rivers flowing over millions of years carve deep valleys and canyons through rock layers by erosion. This is the correct pairing of a land formation with the geological force that creates it.
factClaim: Rivers cut through rock layers over time to form deep valleys and canyons.

subject: science
prompt: A student captures several insects in a garden and studies them: a ladybug has its shell cracked, a butterfly has the typical yellow-and-black striped pattern of its species, a grasshopper has all six legs intact, a beetle has green coloring. Which characteristic is most likely an ACQUIRED trait (not inherited)?
optionA: The ladybug's cracked shell
optionB: The butterfly's yellow-and-black stripes
optionC: The grasshopper's six legs
optionD: The beetle's green coloring
explanation: A cracked shell is an injury or damage that the ladybug acquired during its life, not a trait passed down genetically. The stripe pattern, number of legs, and body color are inherited traits determined by genetics.
factClaim: Acquired traits result from injuries or experiences during an organism's life, while inherited traits are passed down through genes.

subject: science
prompt: A gardener tests how quickly water drains through different soil types. Starting with 200 mL of water poured on each soil sample: Sandy soil drains 180 mL through and retains 20 mL, Clay soil drains 60 mL through and retains 140 mL, Loamy soil drains 150 mL through and retains 50 mL, Gravel drains 195 mL through and retains 5 mL. The gardener wants to plant a vegetable garden that needs soil that does NOT hold too much water. Which two soil types would be best for this garden?
optionA: Sandy soil and clay soil
optionB: Sandy soil and gravel
optionC: Gravel and loamy soil
optionD: Loamy soil and clay soil
explanation: Sandy soil and gravel both drain water very quickly (retaining only 20 mL and 5 mL respectively), which prevents excess water buildup. These are ideal for plants that prefer drier conditions. Clay holds too much water.
factClaim: Sandy soil and gravel drain water quickly, preventing excessive moisture retention.

subject: science
prompt: A student pours equal volumes of water and honey into a clear jar, stirs the mixture for ten seconds, and then lets it rest for five minutes. After resting, the honey settles to the bottom and the water sits on top, forming two distinct layers. Which conclusion best describes this observation?
optionA: Honey is less dense than water
optionB: Water is less dense than honey
optionC: Honey and water are equally dense
optionD: Density cannot be determined from this experiment
explanation: When two liquids are mixed, the less dense liquid floats on top and the denser liquid sinks to the bottom. Since water floats above the honey, water is less dense than honey.
factClaim: When liquids separate by density, the less dense liquid floats on top of the more dense liquid.

subject: science
prompt: Large coal deposits are found underground in certain regions of the world. How did these coal deposits most likely form?
optionA: Heat from deep within Earth transformed rocks into coal
optionB: Dead plants from ancient forests were buried, compressed, and heated over millions of years
optionC: Animals that died millions of years ago were crushed and turned into coal
optionD: Coal formed when volcanoes erupted and deposited dark ash
explanation: Coal forms from the remains of plants (especially trees) that lived in ancient swamps. Over millions of years, these plants were buried under layers of sediment, compressed, and heated, transforming into coal.
factClaim: Coal formed from dead plants buried and compressed over millions of years.

subject: science
prompt: A student builds a simple rocket by taping an inflated balloon to a plastic straw attached to a car-shaped object. When the balloon is released, air rushes backward out of the straw, pushing the car forward. Which statement correctly describes the motion of the car based on this action-reaction pair?
optionA: The car moves in the same direction as the escaping air
optionB: The car moves in the opposite direction from the escaping air
optionC: The car only moves because the balloon becomes lighter as air escapes
optionD: The car does not move because forces inside the balloon cancel out
explanation: According to Newton's third law, for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. When air is expelled backward from the balloon, the car experiences a reaction force pushing it forward, in the opposite direction.
factClaim: Newton's third law states that action and reaction forces are equal and opposite, causing the car to move opposite to the expelled air.

subject: science
prompt: A student is given three objects: a brass key, an aluminum foil square, and a steel bolt. The student is asked to identify properties that ALL THREE objects share because they are metals. Which properties do all three metal objects have in common?
optionA: They bend easily, they are attracted to magnets, they conduct electricity
optionB: They dissolve in water, they are shiny, they float
optionC: They conduct electrical energy, they conduct thermal energy, they do not dissolve in water
optionD: They are attracted to magnets, they are heavy, they break easily
explanation: All metals conduct both electrical and thermal energy well. All three objects (brass, aluminum, steel) share these properties. Not all metals are magnetic (brass and aluminum are not magnetic), and not all are equally bendable or heavy.
factClaim: Common properties of all metals include conducting electrical energy and thermal energy, and not dissolving in water.

subject: science
prompt: A fast-growing, non-native water plant now grows in many lakes and can quickly spread across the entire water surface. Which effect will most likely occur when this invasive plant completely covers the surface of a lake?
optionA: Fish will have more places to hide and will increase in number
optionB: Less sunlight will be able to reach the aquatic plants growing underwater
optionC: All the native water plants will migrate to other lakes
optionD: Aquatic animals will gain a new food source and grow larger
explanation: When the invasive plant covers the lake surface, it blocks sunlight from reaching native aquatic plants below. This reduces their ability to photosynthesize and disrupts the ecosystem's food chain.
factClaim: Invasive plants covering water surfaces block sunlight needed by underwater plants for photosynthesis.

subject: science
prompt: Students want to investigate how surface texture affects the speed at which objects slide. Which experimental design will BEST test the effect of surface texture while controlling all other variables?
optionA: Release two different-sized balls from the same height on the same smooth surface
optionB: Roll a ball down three different ramps with different angles from the same starting point with the same force
optionC: Roll the same ball down a smooth surface, a rough surface, and a carpeted surface from the same starting point and same height with the same force
optionD: Drop a ball from different heights onto the same surface and measure how far it bounces
explanation: A good controlled experiment changes only ONE variable (surface texture in this case) while keeping all other variables constant (same ball, same starting point, same height, same force). Option C correctly tests only surface texture while controlling other factors.
factClaim: A controlled experiment tests one variable while keeping all other conditions constant.
